title: Chat list
summary: Shows the chats of the current account, newest activity first, from the SDK room list service. One screen with two scopes: Conversas (DMs and the Pedidos row) and Grupos (rooms with more than two members), ADR 0053. An account can turn on Mural (ADR 0246): Conversas then shows DMs and groups as tiles sized by a score that the phone computes.

roomId.description: The Matrix room ID. Stable key for the row.

name.description: The display name the SDK computes for the room.

avatarUrl.description: mxc URL of the room or DM avatar.

lastMessage.description: Plain-text preview of the row's latest event: the SDK latest event, or a newer message of the local timeline (see the row text note).

sealMark.description: DM only: BipeCompanySeals.mark of the other person (person-profile notes), after the name. Absent in a group.

isOfficial.description: A DM whose other person's full user ID is in registries/official-accounts.json: the row shows the Bipe badge after the name (bipe_badge_official, label bipe_badge_official_a11y). Never from a name or a handle.

isLowPriority.description: The SDK RoomInfo.isLowPriority tag state for archive synchronization (chat-archive).

isFavourite.description: The SDK RoomInfo.isFavourite tag state (m.favourite). A favourite shows in the favourites row, not in the list below it.

tier.description: 1, 2, 3 or 4 from BipeHomeScore.plan. A chat with a null tier has no tile and is only in the plain list.

reason.description: From BipeHomeScore.plan. mention shows bipe_chat_mural_reason_mention, unanswered shows bipe_chat_mural_reason_unanswered. Tier 2 shows it; every tier's screen reader label reads it.

of.description: The preview text of one message, as in the row text note.

messages.description: The newest messages of the local timeline that the tile shows, oldest first. Their number comes from the tier (Mural tiles note).

draft.description: First tile only: the saved composer draft of the room, shown with bipe_app_chat_list_draft and put in the reply field.

phase.description: loading: the first sync has not listed the rooms yet. empty: the account has no chats. loaded: chats is not empty.

chats.description: The chats, in the order the room list service gives (newest activity first).

scope.description: conversas: rooms with two members, plus the Pedidos row at the top. grupos: rooms with more than two members.

favourites.description: The favourites of the current scope that are not archived, in the favourites order (see notes). Empty hides the row.

reorderingFavourites.description: The favourites row is in reorder mode: cells drag to a new position, tap does not open a chat. Starts false; the chat-row-actions reorderFavourites item sets it, bipe_chat_favourites_reorder_done clears it.

muralEnabled.description: The Mural setting of this account, on every device (settings-group row chats.mural, registries/synced-settings.json). Default false. False: the screen works as in the rest of this spec.

muralTiles.description: Mural on, scope conversas: the tiles in BipeHomeScore.plan order, with a non-null tier. Empty while Mural is off.

muralShowsList.description: Mural on: the person opened the plain list with bipe_chat_mural_view_list. Starts false.

muralReplyText.description: The text of the reply field on the first tile. Starts with the saved draft of the room, if there is one.

loadMore.effect: Asks the room list service for the next page when the last row is on screen, and again while a new page adds rooms. The empty state asks too. No button: paging is automatic.

favourite.description: true adds the m.favourite tag, false removes it.

setFavourite.effect: Room.setIsFavourite on that room in this account. Adding a favourite also puts its room ID last in the favourites order; removing one removes its room ID from the order. The chat moves to the favourites row or back to the list when the room list updates.

toIndex.description: Its new position in the favourites of the current scope, 0 first.

moveFavourite.effect: Moves the favourite in the current scope and writes the favourites order (Client.setAccountData). The other scope's rooms keep their positions. The row shows the new order at once.

openMuralList.effect: Sets muralShowsList. The plain list shows every chat of the Conversas and Grupos rooms, a chat with no tile too, and no tile. Back returns to the tiles.

roomId.description: The room of the first tile.

text.description: The text in the reply field.

replyFromTile.effect: Sends text with the send rules of composer (Timeline.send). Clears the reply field and the saved draft of the room. An empty text sends nothing. A failed send keeps the text and shows the composer's failed state. After the send, the chat is read: the same public receipt and flag as setUnread, so its unread score goes.

notes: MZ decision 25 Oct 2026 (bipe#577): no current-account avatar in the top bar. Você shows the current account (spec voce). This replaces the top-bar avatar of ADR 0135 point 5 for Bipe Next.

Row date (MZ decision 25 Oct 2026, bipe#592): every row with a known event shows its date. The SDK latest event (Room.latestEvent) skips encrypted events that this phone cannot decrypt (matrix-sdk latest_events: m.room.encrypted is never a candidate), so a room whose recent events are all undecryptable has no latest event. The time of an event is not encrypted: such a row takes origin_server_ts of the newest message-like event of the room's local timeline (Room.timeline, the first Timeline.addListener update, no pagination, no network), undecryptable events included; else the newest local event of any kind. Bipe logic: BipeRowActivity (BipeKit, libraries/bipe). Read it again when the room changes in the room list. Rows with no local event stay without a date until the SDK has one.

Row text (MZ, 26 Oct 2026, bipe#592 follow-up): the SDK picks its latest event once, when the event arrives. A message that arrives before its room key is m.room.encrypted at that moment and is never a candidate, and nothing recomputes the latest event after the timeline decrypts it, so the row kept an older event (for example the own join, "You accepted the invite"). Every row also reads its local timeline (the same read as the row date). When the newest message-like local event is newer than the SDK latest event, or there is no SDK latest event, the row takes that event's time and its preview (text, media kind label, sticker, call kind or missed call, or bipe_app_timeline_undecryptable while it still does not decrypt). Otherwise the SDK latest event stays. A call (m.rtc.notification, m.call.invite) is message-like: the SDK takes it as a latest event too. Only an event with a preview gives the row its text (MZ, 27 Oct 2026, build 205: rows whose last event was a call showed a date and no text). A deleted message, a call membership change or an SDK latest event without a preview never blanks the text: the row keeps the newest preview it has. The row order stays the SDK's. Bipe logic: BipeRowActivity.

Row text, own and membership (MZ, 27 Oct 2026): an own message, sticker, media or call shows as bipe_chat_list_own_preview ("You: <preview>"). A message, sticker, media or call from another member of a group shows the sender first: "<name>: <preview>" (MZ, 7 November 2026), with the same person name as the timeline, on iOS, Android, web and Mac. A DM shows the preview alone. No new string: the name, a colon and a space come before the preview, as in a group notification. A missed call and a membership line never take the prefix. A join, an accepted invite, a leave or the room creation shows as a line when it is the newest local event: bipe_dm_joined_by_you, bipe_dm_joined, bipe_dm_left_by_you, bipe_dm_left, bipe_dm_created_by_you, bipe_dm_created in a DM; bipe_group_state_event_room_join_by_you, _join, _leave_by_you, _leave, _created_by_you, _created in a group. Other membership changes (invite, kick, ban, knock, profile) give the row no text. The SDK never takes a join as its latest event, so the local timeline read gives these lines.

Keep a known latest-activity timestamp and its preview visible while the SDK briefly has no latest-event preview or a changed room is read again (bipe#590), scoped to this account session. The date label must have room beside a long chat title. Do not invent today's date for an unknown event or wait for network to draw the list. Truly unknown times remain unknown until local SDK data arrives.
bipe_app_chat_list_unread is the accessibility label of the badge. The count comes in already formatted.

A chat with an unread mention (RoomInfo.numUnreadMentions > 0) shows an @ mark before the count, so a mention differs by shape, not only by colour (bipe#497). The badge's accessibility label adds bipe_a11y_mention.
Message requests, filters, search, invites and Bipe trust badges are later issues. The slice lists joined rooms only.

Official accounts (ADR 0117, bipe-chat/bipe#384): the Bipe badge is a small capsule with the text bipe_badge_official in the verified colours, read as bipe_badge_official_a11y. It shows only for a DM whose other person (the hero user ID) is exactly a user ID in registries/official-accounts.json (BipeRegistries.officialAccountIDs / officialAccountIds). A display name, a handle or a lookalike user ID on another server never shows it. A group never shows it, except the account's own news room (news room mark below). The same rule holds in the chat header (chat-timeline) and person-profile. Bipe logic: BipeOfficialAccounts.isOfficial (BipeKit, libraries/bipe).

DM avatars show photos from the SDK, with initials when absent. A company avatar is a rounded square based on GET /v1/accounts/{userId}/type (ADR 0132), regardless of verification. Group avatars are the room avatar (m.room.avatar). Group avatar (bipe-chat/bipe#1004): a group with no m.room.avatar shows up to 3 other members as overlapping circles inside the group circle, from RoomInfo.heroes without the own user (userId, displayName, avatarUrl). Each member shows the photo or the initial. One member: that member only. No members: the group initial. The same holds in search, the favourites row, the timeline header and group-details.

The SDK room-list order is authoritative: it incorporates the server recency stamp even while an event preview is missing. Never re-sort all rows by optional locally cached latest-event timestamps. Preserve filtered-list order as well; append out-of-page archived rooms deterministically.

Request SDK latest-event hydration for displayed and loaded-page rooms with RoomListService.subscribeToRooms. In SDK26.08.11 this REPLACES existing subscriptions, so one coordinator per immutable account session must combine owners from all active lists, including Unread, groups, requests and search. Releasing one owner must preserve other lists. Close on sign-out. Publish cached rows before background hydration; no network or decryption gate on opening the app.

A group uses RoomInfo.displayName, including explicit room names, before hero/profile/localpart fallbacks. An absent hero never overrides an available SDK name with Unnamed chat. Do not read another client database or infer a missing date from current time.

A DM (RoomInfo.isDm, ADR 0141) always shows the other person: the name is the hero display name, then RoomInfo.displayName only when it is not the room's own m.room.name (RoomInfo.rawName), then the hero's @handle, then bipe_dm_no_name. Never the Matrix ID or its localpart (README, People names). The photo is the hero avatar only, never RoomInfo.avatarUrl (m.room.avatar): without one the row shows initials. The same rule holds in search, the share picker, the timeline header, person-profile and notifications.

MZ supplied screenshots of build32 and the previous app on 23 October 2026: list dates/previews are missing on several rows, room ordering differs and a named chat appears unnamed. These are conversation-list parity reports (bipe#590), distinct from individual message clock footers. Use synthetic fixtures in committed regression tests; never publish personal screenshot contents.
Brand marks (ADR 0162, spec brand-mark): a DM row with a reseller shows the first verified mark's line under the name, short and on one line, with bipe_brand_mark_more for the others.

News room (MZ decision 27 Oct 2026, bipe#809): Novidades do Bipe is a named room, not a DM. bipe-api makes it without is_direct, so RoomInfo.isDm is false and the room takes the non-DM path everywhere: the row, the chat header, search and the notification title show RoomInfo.displayName (its m.room.name, bipe_news_room_name) and the room avatar, and the row is in the Grupos scope. News room mark (MZ decision 2 Nov 2026, bipe#978, replaces the no-badge rule): the app keeps the room_id of GET /v1/me/news on the phone for the account. The row and the chat header of that exact room show the Bipe badge (bipe_badge_official) and the name bipe_news_room_name in the app language, not its m.room.name. No other group shows the badge. The DM rule (ADR 0141) does not change. Rooms made before the fix are in the account's m.direct. Once per account on each phone, after the first sync, the app reads room_id from GET /v1/me/news and, when the room is joined, removes that room ID from the server copy of m.direct (Client.setAccountData; a user whose list becomes empty goes) and remembers that it ran. It waits while the room is only an invite, because joining an invite that says is_direct adds the room to m.direct again. A failure, or news_unavailable, tries again at the next start or return to the foreground. subscribed false counts as done. The support room stays a DM: it shows the support account's name, which bipe-api sets to bipe_support_room_name.

Favourites row (MZ, 27 Oct 2026, bipe#673): favourite chats (m.favourite, RoomInfo.isFavourite) show at the top of their scope as a grid of large avatars, three per line, with the name under each avatar on one line. A favourite does not show again in the list below. An unread favourite shows the accent dot on its avatar, and its accessibility label adds bipe_chat_unread_state. Tap opens the chat; long press opens the same chat-row-actions menu. The row is the first item of the list, above the history banner, the first-list cards, the requests row and group invites (MZ, 27 Oct 2026, build 233: under the invites it looked wrong). It scrolls with the chats. The group's accessibility label is bipe_chat_favourites. Order: the favourites order below, not the room list order. No limit: more than three wrap to the next line. The archived list never shows the row. The tag syncs, so a favourite set on one phone shows on every phone of the account. Default chosen: per scope (Conversas shows favourite DMs, Grupos favourite groups, a company account's single list shows both), because a scope shows only its own chats everywhere else. MZ can overrule. A favourite outside the loaded pages still shows: a second room list stream with the Favourite filter (All of Joined, NonSpace, Favourite, DeduplicateVersions) finds it, the same way chat-archive finds archives.

Favourites order (MZ, 3 Nov 2026: recency order moved the avatars at every new message, so the grid had no fixed places). The user sets the order; a new message never moves a favourite. The order is the global account data event registries/chat-favourites.json orderEventType (BipeRegistries.chatFavouritesOrderEventType), content { "rooms": [room IDs, first first] }, so every phone of the account shows the same order. Not the m.favourite tag order: the SDK writes it but cannot read it back. Rules (display, new favourite last, removal, other-scope positions, orderMax, malformed content, failed write) are in the registry $comment. Read the event when the list starts and when the favourite rooms change. Reorder mode: chat-row-actions reorderFavourites starts it. The row then shows bipe_chat_favourites_reorder_hint above the grid and a bipe_chat_favourites_reorder_done button; the unread dot stays; tap does nothing; a drag of a cell moves it to the cell under the finger, and the row writes the order when the drag ends. Each cell has the accessibility actions bipe_chat_favourite_move_earlier and bipe_chat_favourite_move_later (not on the first or last cell), which run moveFavourite one step. Leaving the list, changing scope or a row with fewer than two favourites ends reorder mode. Default chosen: an explicit mode, not drag straight from the long press, because the long press already opens the menu on both platforms. MZ can overrule.

Android only (bipe#823): when the permission or battery check of notification-checkup fails, a banner above the list shows bipe_app_notification_checkup_banner with bipe_app_notification_checkup_fix (opens notification-checkup) and a close button (bipe_app_close). Closing it hides it for 7 days on this phone.

Mural setting (ADR 0246, bipe-chat/bipe#1044): the switch bipe_chats_mural with the footer bipe_chats_mural_footer, in Configurações > Conversas e mídia (settings-group row chats.mural). Default off. The app stores it per account in the account data of registries/synced-settings.json and keeps a copy on the device. Turning it on or off changes the Conversas tab at once. With Mural off, nothing else on this screen changes.

Mural scope (ADR 0246): with Mural on, the Conversas tab shows DMs and groups together, as the company todas scope does, and its badge adds gruposAttention (spec app-tabs). The Grupos tab does not change and keeps the plain list. The Pedidos row stays where it is. A request gets no score and no tile. An archived chat gets no score and no tile. The favourites row does not show in Mural: a favourite adds to the score only. The first-list cards and the banners stay above the tiles.

Mural score (ADR 0246): every tile comes from BipeHomeScore.plan (Swift, Kotlin) or homePlan (web, generated lib/home-score.mjs with registries.json homeScore). registries/home-score.json holds the formula, the weights and the limits; test-vectors/home-score.json checks them. No platform keeps a second copy or changes a tier. No score or signal leaves the device: not to bipe-api, not to account data, not to analytics, not to another device. Two devices of one person can show different tiles.

Mural inputs (BipeHomeChat): id is the room ID. kind: group when the room is not a DM (the news room too); company when GET /v1/accounts/{userId}/type says company (ADR 0132); else person. hasSeal: sealMark is company; companySuspended counts as no seal. official: isOfficial, and true for the news room (news room mark note), so that it stays at the official cap. favourite: isFavourite. muted: the RoomNotificationMode of the room is mute (spec chat-notifications). mentioned: RoomInfo.numUnreadMentions > 0; a reply to the person counts through its m.mentions. unreadCount: as in the row. lastFromOther: the newest message-like event of the local timeline has another sender; false when unknown. minutesSinceActivity: whole minutes, rounded down, from the row date (lastActivity) to now; null when the row date is unknown. trustWarning: false in step 1, no model runs. modelAttention and modelDue: absent in step 1.

messagesPerWeek (ADR 0246, default chosen for bipe-chat/bipe#1044): the count of message-like events, from anyone, with origin_server_ts in the last 7 days (registries/home-score.json tie.windowDays), in the local timeline of the room. It is the same read as the row date note (Room.timeline, the first Timeline.addListener update): no network, no pagination. Undecryptable events count, because their time is not encrypted. A room with no local events counts 0. The count therefore can be lower than the true count, and it never asks the server for more.

Mural tiles (ADR 0246). Tier 1: full width, avatar and name, then messages. The first tile shows the last 3 messages (BipeHomeScore firstTileMessages), the draft if there is one, and a reply field with bipe_chats_message_placeholder that sends with replyFromTile. The second tile shows the last message. Tier 2: half width, avatar, name, reason and one bubble with the last message. Tier 3: one third of the width, avatar, first word of the name, two lines of text. Tier 4: avatar only, in rows that wrap, under the heading bipe_chat_mural_no_news. A person or company name follows README People names. Step 1 shows real messages only, with no gist and no reason from a model. Tap on a tile opens chat-timeline; long press opens chat-row-actions. A tap on the reply field does not open the chat.

Mural grid rules (ADR 0246): the tier sets the tile and nothing else sets it. The last row of a tier stretches, so the grid has no hole. bipe_chat_mural_view_list ends the screen and opens the plain list. Avatar shape, seal and member cluster follow the rules of this spec at every size. Tiles meet the touch target rule (44 pt, 48 dp), Dynamic Type and font scaling. Screen readers read tiles in plan order, with name, reason and unread count (bipe_app_chat_list_unread). The reason already says the mention, so a tile does not add bipe_a11y_mention. Web difference: the web client cannot verify a seal, so hasSeal is false and a sealed company scores as a company without a seal there. A tile does not move during a touch or a scroll: new text and badges show in place, and new tiers and positions apply when the screen is at rest.

Mural improvements (MZ, 5 Nov 2026): this spec is the rule for Mural, not the prototype (branch prototype/home-mural, fixture data). To adopt something from the prototype, change this spec first, then the code. A layout problem (tile content, spacing, grid) changes the Mural notes of this spec, then iOS, Android and web in one PR. An order problem (a chat too large or too small) changes registries/home-score.json and test-vectors/home-score.json only, never one platform, and the PR states the case that caused the change, with no message text. Each note from a device test is one small issue, with a screenshot and the prototype's version of the same screen, and it is not part of steps 2 and 3 of ADR 0246.

Mural model (ADR 0246): steps 2 and 3 are not built. No model runs, and privacy.json and data.json list none. registries/home-score.json keeps the model weights, marked unused-step-1, and the function reads them only when a caller passes model fields. No caller passes them in step 1.

Mac desktop (MZ, 7 November 2026, bipe#1018): apply the own web/iOS row hierarchy: 48 pt avatar, 12 pt gap, headline name and caption date, then subheadline preview and unread/mention/mute indicators. Use the same account-avatar control at the upper left, title and search field. Favourites keep the three-column avatar grid, sync and stable order described above; a member cluster and a real group photo follow the same rules in the list, favourites and timeline header. Do not add an Unread chip or a second favourites representation. The Mac body uses the shared 17 pt iOS/web scale with rounded type and accessibility scaling, instead of the smaller macOS default.
